# `project.serving`

[project](../README.md) · serving

THE BUNDLE'S SERVING CONTRACT — how this bundle spells the relations it serves. A CORE key, deliberately, and not an `x-` extension: the serving-name convention was the single most-replicated finding of the eight-walk ingestion experiment, and every walk that tried to declare it reached for `x-serving-naming`, which this schema rejects (additionalProperties:false, no ^x- pattern) and which tools/check_extension_keys.py PROHIBITS as MAC012. The framework was therefore teaching, in a gate's failure message, the one declaration two other mechanisms refuse — opposite policies in one framework, which is a defect to remove rather than a tension to document. Removing it means the convention must have a home the core defines, validates and a gate reads: this one. Enforced by tools/check_served_name_distinct.py.

### `naming`

*object* · optional · [has its own keys →](naming/README.md)

The serving-name convention THIS bundle keeps. Structural on purpose — a marker plus a role table, from which the gate DERIVES the acceptance test. It is deliberately NOT a free-text regex or name template: an unverifiable string is exactly the weakness that got `x-` keys ruled out, and a convention nothing can check is worse than none, because the manifest then claims a guarantee nothing enforces. Declaring this block makes the full build-shape `<role>_<marker>_<business noun>` REQUIRED and checked; declaring nothing leaves the published DEFAULT in force, which still closes the role table but does not require the marker.

Its own keys: [`project.serving.naming`](naming/README.md)
